title: Joint custody arrangements - are Indian courts finally adopting them
p1:
Can a child truly belong to only one parent after a separation?

A growing number of custody discussions in India are challenging this old assumption.
p2: Many people believe custody means one parent wins and the other loses. But courts are increasingly focusing on what benefits the child most, including arrangements where both parents share responsibilities and time.
p3:
Joint custody does not always mean equal time with both parents. It can mean shared decision-making, regular involvement, and ensuring the child continues to have a meaningful relationship with both parents. Indian courts have started recognising this approach in suitable cases, though it is not yet an automatic rule. The child's welfare remains the deciding factor.

The key takeaway: custody is not about parental rights alone, but about creating stability and care for the child.
conclusion: Do you think Indian courts should move towards joint custody as the default option after separation, or should every case be decided differently?
